text: If docs/components/ files exist in agent_workspace but Component artifacts are not registered and synthesis:done is not applied, the synthesis is incomplete — a prior script scaffolded the structure without filling Overviews or finishing the pipeline handoff; the Synthesizer agent should complete the remaining steps rather than passing.

The file-documenter watchdog fires even when source files are absent from agent_workspace — if the AEE extraction pipeline committed only KB records (not source files), the file-documenter cannot proceed and correctly returns [PASS] on every watchdog cycle; fix requires the extraction pipeline to also commit source files or a pipeline design change to allow documentation from KB records alone.

The file-documenter requires 'Extract Log' registered via aee-artifact, not just the raw .aee/extract-log.jsonl file — if only the raw file exists, aee-artifact path 'Extract Log' returns not-found and the documenter correctly returns [PASS].
When agent_workspace diverges from origin (forced update), use git reset --hard origin/agent_workspace to resync — ff-only pull will abort and leave the agent on a stale branch.

A force-push to agent_workspace clears all aee-artifact registrations — after a force-push all four required artifacts (Component Index, Security Chains, Extract Log, Security Log) will be missing and verifier must [PASS] until upstream agents re-register them.

When agent_workspace has diverged due to a forced remote update (non-fast-forward), use git reset --hard origin/agent_workspace to sync cleanly before running the readiness gate — git pull --ff-only will abort.
When agent_workspace has diverged from origin, do a hard reset (git reset --hard origin/agent_workspace) before beginning any analysis — ff-only pull will fail on a diverged branch.

artifacts.jsonl in .agent-studio/ is an append-only JSONL file shared by all agents; rebase conflicts must be resolved by keeping all entries from both sides, never discarding another agent's registrations.

When the license scanner finds SPDX headers only in application source files (not in LICENSE*/NOTICE*/vendor trees), the correct outcome is an empty component inventory — do not report source-file header notices as bundled component licenses.

When rebasing against a fast-moving agent_workspace shared by many concurrent agents, artifacts.jsonl merge conflicts are common — always merge all agents' entries (do not discard any existing lines) and continue the rebase rather than aborting.

When the user requests a workspace reset and re-clone, force-reset agent_workspace to main with 'git reset --hard origin/main && git push --force origin agent_workspace' — this clears all pipeline artifacts and pipeline state so a fresh extraction cycle can begin.

When aee-artifact registrations are cleared (e.g. after a force-push), the file-documenter can still proceed by reading the raw .aee/extract-log.jsonl and .aee/kb/ files directly — the artifact path() call failing is a readiness gate for unattended runs, not a hard blocker when the user explicitly triggers a run.

When registering 1000+ artifacts, write entries directly to .agent-studio/artifacts.jsonl in JSONL format rather than calling aee-artifact add per file — the tool format is {artifact, path, by, commit, ts} and git add staging is done once after the bulk write.

When agent_workspace is force-updated and the local branch has diverged, git rebase --continue requires explicit git identity flags (-c user.email/user.name) if no git config is set in the environment.

The dependency-analyzer's /src scan target does not exist as an absolute path; the actual source tree is at test-repo/src/ — osv-scanner commands using /src will fail with 'no such file or directory'.

When git rebase --continue fails with 'Committer identity unknown', set GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL and GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL env vars for that invocation — git config is not writable in the agent environment.

When git pull --rebase conflicts on artifacts.jsonl during a push loop, resolve by keeping all JSON lines from both sides, deduplicating by content, then continue the rebase — never discard any agent's registrations.

When agent_workspace diverges repeatedly during push (concurrent agents), use git fetch + git reset --hard origin/agent_workspace, re-apply changes, then retry gh-as-agent push — do not attempt repeated rebases without resetting first.
aee-emit is deprecated (#2578) — apply pipeline outcome labels directly with 'gh issue edit <n> --add-label <label> --repo <owner/repo>'.

When the security reviewer encounters add/add conflicts in findings files during rebase (multiple agents committing to agent_workspace concurrently), resolve findings.json conflicts with --ours and all other .aee/ data files with --theirs, then deduplicate artifacts.jsonl — this pattern recurs on every multi-agent concurrent push.

When all security findings across a batch are empty (zero-byte __init__.py files), the Cross-File Security Correlator correctly produces an empty chains artifact with zero confirmed/partial/terminated chains — this is not an error, it is the expected outcome for such a batch.

When the git remote is configured for SSH but the environment has no SSH access, switch to HTTPS with 'git remote set-url origin https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git' before any fetch or push — GH_TOKEN is already set for HTTPS auth.

When the quality-analyzer batch has 1000+ files and 50+ rule groups, process groups first with a scripted pass (drop style groups, keep metric candidates, apply rule heuristics) then target the manual pass on the top-10 highest-CCN files and non-grouped candidates with rules B006/W0102/W0715/B023 — these are the rules most likely to be missed by the script.

W0715 'Exception arguments suggest string formatting might be intended' is a high-value rule for Nova: the codebase uses NovaException.__init__(message=None, **kwargs) which only accepts one positional arg, so raise SomeNovaException('msg %s', value) will TypeError at call time — always keep W0715 in KEEP_RULES for non-grouped candidates.
